alt: Outside the school are external factors: family income, home resources, parents’ attitudes and culture, the focus of this sub-section. Inside the school are internal factors: setting, labelling and pupil subcultures, covered mainly in 3.4.4. A note says to look for patterns between groups, not individual cases.
caption: Sort every explanation: from outside the school, or from inside it?

alt: Bar chart: compared with a working-class boy, a service-class boy had four times the chance of being at school at 16, eight times at 17, ten times at 18 and eleven times the chance of attending university. Below: the gap widens, challenges meritocracy, but the sample was male only and educated long ago.
caption: The longer education goes on, the wider the class gap becomes.

alt: Three cards. Material deprivation blames lack of money, such as no laptop or quiet room. Cultural deprivation blames working-class family values and language. Cultural capital blames schools for rewarding middle-class culture. Critics of cultural deprivation say working-class culture is different, not deficient. Below, free school meal eligibility as an indicator.
caption: Cultural deprivation blames the home; cultural capital blames the school.

after: ## Ball on parental choice and competition between schools
alt: Three rows. Privileged or skilled choosers, mostly middle class, had the money, time and knowledge to research, visit, appeal and travel. Semi-skilled choosers fall in between. Disconnected choosers, mostly working class, tended to choose the nearest school. Choice that looks equal is unequal in practice.
caption: Parents with more resources make more effective school choices.

alt: Two cards. Girls’ achievement rose because of feminism, shown by Sharpe’s study, equal opportunities laws and the national curriculum, and changes in jobs and family. Some boys fall behind because manual jobs declined and some masculine identities see hard work as uncool. Below, subject choice remains gendered, linked to the glass ceiling.
caption: Explain both sides: why girls rose and why some boys fall behind.

alt: Three overlapping circles for class, gender and ethnicity. Where free school meal eligibility, being a boy and being white British meet are some of the lowest-attaining pupils in England. Below, a reminder that factors combine and that part of an ethnic gap may be a class gap.
caption: Factors combine, so judge how much of one gap is really another.
